label: input y at original positions 3-5, boosted by a preceding y or first token o/f/j
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit (~0.03% of steps). 99% of activation mass is in the original phase, and 93% of it is on steps whose input is the letter y; a few weak activations fall on s, v, l, and <DEL> right after an early y. It fires only at positions t=3..6, mostly 3..5, and never at t<3 or in the copy phase. Most y inputs do not trigger it (precision 1.7% for y in the original phase), so firing depends on context. It is more likely and stronger when the previous input was also y (yy runs give the top activations, with the second or third y the strongest) and when the sequence starts with o, f, or j (also p and z). The chosen predicate (y at t=3..5 AND (first token o/f/j OR previous token y)) gets dev F1 0.37 and mass recall 0.77. Precision stays low (~0.25), so the exact gating context is not fully captured. It does not fire on other letters, digits, or the copy phase.
